newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stability pact a cornerstone of EMU - Duisenberg.
newsitem.headline: Stability pact a cornerstone of EMU - Duisenberg.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Thursday the stability and growth pact agreed at the EU's Dublin summit in December was one of the cornerstones of European economic and monetary union (EMU).

"It will establish a foundation of fiscal stability under the operations of the European Central Bank (ECB), and thereby contribute to the impact of its policies," he said in a speech at the Erasmus University in Rotterdam.
Duisenberg will take over in July as head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner of the ECB.

Duisenberg noted that the pact was aimed at ensuring EU states maintained fiscal discipline both before and after the planned launch of the EU's single currency in 1999 by running only a small budget deficit or indeed a budget surplus.

"...the reasons why we need a pact for stability and growth in EMU may be explained by my fundamental belief that a lack of fiscal discipline would negatively affect the ability of the European Central Bank to achieve its primary objective to maintain price stability," he said.
Duisenberg said he favoured a return to the low budget deficits or budget surpluses which were common in Europe in the 1960s.
From 1970 to 1995 average government debt in the 15 EU countries rose from 34.6 percent of GDP to 71.7 percent and was accompanied by a quadrupling of average unemployment, he said.
